articles.title: Zoho Co-Founder Sridhar Vembu Says No Usual Pay Hike This Year Amid Rising AI Costs
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 13 (IANS) Zoho's Chief Scientist and Co-founder Sridhar Vembu on Tuesday said that we have cut down on our marketing budget and told employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year. The business outlook for software is uncertain and AI has raised costs dramatically, he wrote in a post on X. Vembu further noted that there has been four-fold increase in server prices needed for data centres and AI usage is increasing rapidly, leading to much higher expenses which company is trying to control. On top of that is challenging geopolitical backdrop, he added. "We have cut down on our marketing budget. We have also told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year. I have apologized for not being able to avoid this," Vembu said in a post. "We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs but outlook for software jobs in general is grim. We have not been growing our employee count for 18 months now," he said. Most of employees understand situation and I am thankful to them, he added. "We are in middle of reinventing ourselves. Next 3-5 years will decide how our reinvention has worked. Please pray for us," Vembu said. Earlier in May, Vembu cautioned that soaring valuations of world's largest technology companies, fuelled by investor enthusiasm around artificial intelligence, exhibit characteristics of market bubble that could eclipse dot-com era. He highlighted price-to-sales ratios of major technology firms, arguing that current market valuations appear increasingly detached from underlying business fundamentals. Moreover, he had cited companies such as Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Micron Technology, noting that several are trading at elevated multiples of their annual revenues. To underline concerns, Vembu referenced remarks made by Scott McNealy following collapse of dot-com bubble in early 2000s. McNealy had argued that investors paying ten times company's annual revenue would need extraordinary performance and profitability over many years to justify such valuations, he added. Software business outlook uncertain, AI raised costs dramatically: Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu. (This report has been published as part of the auto-generated syndicate wire feed. Apart from the headline, no editing has been done in the copy by ABP Live.)

articles.title: UPI MDR Deferred: Who Pays, How Much, And What Changes After Diwali
articles.description: Shopkeepers and businesses gearing up for the festive rush will have a little more breathing room before new charges on certain UPI payments kick in. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) said on Tuesday that the rollout of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions has been deferred until after Diwali. Festive season behind the pause According to an NPCI statement, the UPI and Services Steering Committee took the decision on 13 October, with the festive season in mind. The revised rates will now come into effect immediately after Diwali, on a date that will be notified separately. The move pushes back the rollout that had been planned for 15 October, giving merchants and payment service providers additional time to prepare before the new framework applies. Who will pay, and how much Under the revised framework, a flat MDR of Rs 5 will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in select merchant categories, including railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel. For larger merchant payments above Rs 2,000, a charge of 0.4% will apply, capped at Rs 300, as per the earlier framework outlined by NPCI. The impact, however, is expected to be narrow. Around 4% of merchant transactions are likely to fall under the framework, while more than 95% of person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions will stay outside it. Small merchants operating under the person-to-person merchant (P2PM) model will continue to pay zero MDR. What it means for everyday users For individual users, NPCI said there will be no monthly quota or cap on free UPI transactions, and payments covered by the free framework will continue without any MDR charge. Banks have also been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass the cost on to customers, so consumers are not expected to face an extra charge for paying through UPI under the revised structure. Where the money will go Under the new structure, 5% of total MDR collections will be set aside for a dedicated fund to support UPI acceptance among small merchants. The rest of the MDR revenue will be shared among participants across the UPI ecosystem and is expected to help fund the expansion of the payment system, cybersecurity and innovation, according to NPCI. The revised rates are also expected to remain lower than the charges applicable to cards and digital wallets, the statement said.
